requirements_slice.system_goal: Make the Week screen execution-ready as a strict WeekBrief-driven surface with explicit DTO/UI mapping, explainable structure, bounded write scope, and deterministic verification.

in_scope.item: Week top-layer structure for `frontend/app/week/page.tsx` driven by `WeekBrief` / `WeekBriefEnvelope` via `frontend/lib/week-brief.ts`.
Explainability exposure for summary/theme, day cards, domains, major factors, premium/report CTA, and fallback transparency.
Stable semantic mapping from canonical backend `week_brief` into user-visible Week/UI blocks; legacy `week_map` is not a user-facing substitute for `/week`.
Execution packet guidance for write scope, frozen scope, acceptance criteria, verification, and wave ordering.

out_of_scope.item: New product features or new business logic for week scoring.
Rewriting backend deterministic calculations in `backend/app/services/week_brief_service.py` or `backend/app/services/week_map.py`.
Billing/catalog architecture changes beyond existing CTA/resume wiring.

use_case.summary: User opens `/week` and sees a stable top-layer week surface: one theme/hero, a day-map layer, domain guidance, factor-based explanation, and a clear CTA path.
use_case.scenario: Top block presents one semantic center based on `summary`, `status`, and theme-oriented copy; deep-report markdown is not duplicated into top layer.
Week map renders as ordered day cards with stable day semantics: date, weekday, score/mode/headline, best-for, avoid.
Domain cards and practical guidance show bounded, polished copy derived from DTO fields rather than frontend recomputation.
Primary CTA resolves cleanly to full report when `reportId` exists, otherwise to premium/create flow.

use_case.summary: User can understand why the week is framed this way through visible factor-backed sections, confidence hints, and fallback disclosure.
use_case.scenario: Major factors render as bounded explainability artifacts with label/category/impact explanation rather than raw service payload.
Explainability layer preserves confidence and birth-time usage as support context for telemetry and user trust, without leaking ambiguous technical copy.
Fallback mode is visible through a compact note and preserves usable Week UI instead of degrading into empty/raw JSON states.

use_case.summary: Worker can implement or refine Week UI against frozen semantic coordinates and adapter responsibilities without guessing DTO ownership.
use_case.scenario: If backend returns `week_brief_envelope.data`, adapter uses it as source of truth and keeps envelope/report status semantics stable.
If `week_brief` is absent, `/week` renders an honest empty/in_progress/error state instead of deriving a substitute Week UI from `week_map`.
Loading, error, in-progress, ready, premium/report CTA, and fallback note states are explicitly mapped to visible UI coordinates.

business_invariants.invariant: `WeekBrief` / `WeekBriefEnvelope` remains the canonical top-layer DTO for `/week`.
Backend remains source of truth for week boundaries, scores, domains, and factor logic; frontend only adapts and presents.
Top-layer Week UI MUST not regress into markdown-first or legacy hand-assembled content.
Fallback mode MUST stay premium-enough and informative without exposing raw service keys, debug booleans, or unlocalized labels.
Execution packet MUST freeze semantic coordinates so multiple coder workers can implement without DTO/UI drift.

expected_failure_handling.item: If report lookup returns no canonical `week_forecast` WeekBrief, UI renders empty/create or in-progress state without crashing and without mock/default substitute content.
If `week_brief_envelope.status` is not `ready`, top layer still preserves loading/in-progress/error semantics instead of mislabeling the screen as complete.
If explainability subfields are partially absent, UI omits unavailable detail blocks and preserves the concise first layer.
If full report linkage is absent, CTA gracefully routes to create/premium flow and telemetry surface names stay stable.

known_defects.defect: Week strict DTO is present, but packet-level execution guidance for future refinements is not yet frozen like Today packet.
Week legacy `week_map` is migration/internal baggage only; workers must not reattach it to the primary `/week` product path.
Loading/error/in-progress/fallback/CTA semantics exist in code, but are not yet assembled into one execution-ready docs packet.
Major factors/confidence/fallback transparency are implemented, but semantic UI coordinates are not documented for coder handoff.

success_criteria.criterion: Packet defines stable Week/UI semantic coordinates and DTO ownership for top-layer `/week` work.
Packet explains exact UI mapping for `summary`, `status`, `day_cards`, `domains`, `best_uses`, `risks`, `major_factors`, `premium`, `explainability`, and `cta`.
Packet gives explicit write scope and frozen scope so coder workers stay documentation-aligned and do not expand into unrelated product work.
Packet defines deterministic verification using backend quick pipeline plus targeted week E2E/regression specs.
Packet sequences execution waves in a way that supports safe Week/UI refinement without backend truth-path drift.
